tasks.short: Prepare period-end payroll reports and reconcile payroll payments to bank statements.

steps.what: Export payroll totals and payment details from the {PAYROLL}.
Download bank transactions covering payroll settlement dates.
Match payroll payments to statement entries and calculate differences in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Resolve unmatched payments with the finance team through {EMAIL}.
Prepare the period-end report with totals, explanations, and outstanding differences.
Review outstanding differences and approve the period-end payroll report.

tasks.design: Configured exports from the {PAYROLL} and {BANK} feed a deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, matching payment identifiers, amounts, currencies, and settlement dates. A queue in the {WORKFLOW} presents unresolved items with source records, while a template generates the report in the {DOCS} for approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate exports, inconsistent payment references, and limited implementation capacity left the clerk joining records manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export features and reusable matching code cover most processing. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector and report development; no model is needed for matching.
tasks.still_hard: Aggregated bank debits, rejected payments, reversals, and settlement timing need explicit rules. Missing payment identifiers still require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk establishes why money moved differently from the payroll instruction and gets the responsible team to resolve it.

ambition.what: Weekly decision on which unresolved payroll cash differences need escalation.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports to resolving cash exceptions before close. Proposed new authority is to assign reconciliation cases and escalate overdue differences; payment authority does not change.

reach.task: Explain recurring differences between expected and paid compensation costs.
reach.learn: Pay-component mapping, accrual timing, and benefit settlement schedules.

evidence.claim: Exact-reference bank matching with exceptions routed to people is available in existing software.
Payroll-to-bank reconciliation can use deterministic matching, control totals, and report templates.
The digest contains no documented payroll reconciliation case establishing a realised saving.

assumptions: This baseline uses a clerk-maintained reconciliation between separate payroll and banking records.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The scope prepares reconciliation records; corrections and payment release follow their existing approval processes.
Payroll data remains access-controlled under GDPR, with appropriate retention and audit records.
unknowns: Whether an existing reconciliation feature already covers the full task.
Whether bank entries identify individual payments or only batch totals.
Available export formats, identifiers, access permissions, and approval roles.
Number of legal entities, currencies, bank accounts, and off-cycle runs.
research_questions: Which structured bank formats preserve payroll batch and rejection identifiers?
Which existing reconciliation features handle reversals and split settlements?
new_work: Resolve unmatched items and document accepted timing differences.
Maintain matching rules and payroll-to-bank identifier mappings.
Monitor missing feeds, duplicate imports, and reconciliation control totals.

tasks.short: Check time and wage records, investigate discrepancies, and apply approved payroll corrections.

steps.what: Retrieve approved timesheets, absence records, and draft wage calculations.
Compare hours, rates, deductions, and prior-period pay using checks in the {PAYROLL}.
Read supporting notes and documents to explain each payroll warning.

loop.input: One warning, its source records, relevant approved rules, and supporting free-text notes.
loop.output: A cited explanation, unresolved facts, and a draft clarification request.
loop.check: Every factual claim references a source; code verifies figures and dates. A clerk reviews the explanation.
loop.stop: One draft and one validation repair per warning. Missing sources or failed checks return the case to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rule checks find differences but cannot reliably interpret varied explanations in supporting notes.

steps.what: Clarify disputed hours or pay facts with the employee and line manager.
Decide whether a correction is justified and approve its pay treatment.
Enter approved corrections and rerun payroll checks.

tasks.design: A controlled integration joins approved time and absence data from the {HCM} to draft calculations in the {PAYROLL}, where configured checks produce warnings. A bounded model loop drafts source-linked explanations from notes in the {DOCS}; people settle disputed facts and approve corrections before deterministic posting and rechecking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checks were split between systems, and supporting explanations arrived in varied documents. Interpreting those notes kept even well-structured warnings in a manual queue.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing payroll checks cover arithmetic and period comparisons. A small model loop can prepare explanations, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and approvals.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded work, disputed overtime, retroactive changes, and collective-agreement interpretation remain difficult. A plausible explanation is not proof that pay is correct.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears conflicting accounts, protects the employee's ability to challenge a record, and obtains evidence for a fair correction.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly decisions on unresolved pay corrections before payroll cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving uncertain cases and less time comparing records. No new authority to change pay is assumed; correction approval stays with the authorised payroll role.

reach.task: Investigate recurring disputes about overtime and paid working time.
reach.learn: Collective-agreement interpretation, evidence handling, and fair dispute procedures.

evidence.claim: Nmbrs provides payroll run checks for salary changes.
Nmbrs provides employee-level comparisons across three payroll periods.
Source-linked warning explanations can be drafted in a bounded loop, with numerical validation and human review.
Worker-monitoring uses can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk categories; classification depends on intended use.

assumptions: The target checks payroll correctness and does not score employee performance.
Approved pay rules are available in a maintained, versioned form.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; exception-heavy payrolls retain more human work.
GDPR applies to source records and model processing; national rules govern consultation and employment procedures.
unknowns: Existing check coverage and the frequency of genuine discrepancies.
Where time notes, work charts, and approvals are held.
Applicable collective agreements and correction approval limits.
Permitted model-processing environment and whether consultation is required for this change.
research_questions: Which native checks expose source records and reusable warning identifiers?
How reliably can bounded explanations distinguish missing evidence from a valid pay exception?
new_work: Review drafted explanations and reject unsupported conclusions.
Maintain pay rules, warning thresholds, and source mappings.
Sample cleared warnings for missed errors and monitor false positives.
Maintain model instructions and retest them when rules or document formats change.

tasks.short: Open time submissions, collect completed records, chase missing entries, and obtain approval.

steps.what: Open the pay period and prepare time-entry forms in the {HCM}.
Send employees submission instructions and deadlines through {EMAIL}.
Enter worked hours and submit the timesheet in the {HCM}.
Update a separate {SPREADSHEET} showing received and missing timesheets.
Chase missing submissions and escalate overdue timesheets through {EMAIL}.
Review submitted hours and approve or return the timesheet in the {HCM}.

tasks.design: Configure recurring periods, accessible time-entry forms, submission status, reminders, and approval routing in the {HCM}. Remove the separate {SPREADSHEET} tracker and use the {WORKFLOW} only where native routing is insufficient, with an assisted submission route for employees without desk access.
tasks.previous_blocker: Digital submission often coexists with manual tracking and chasing. Employee access, local working practices, and consultation can matter more than technical complexity.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing self-service and approval features can handle collection without a model. Configuration and small deterministic extensions are cheaper to implement and test with coding assistance.
tasks.still_hard: Employees must still confirm actual hours, and managers must resolve disputed entries. Accessible submission, offline working, GDPR, and national consultation rules need local attention.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk helps employees who cannot use the standard route and notices when missing submissions reflect access or workplace problems.

ambition.what: An assisted time-submission route for employees without desk access.

tasks.altitude: The clerk's week shifts from deadline chasing to access support and unresolved submissions. No new pay or attendance decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Help employees gain access to self-service HR processes.
reach.learn: Accessible form design, identity checks, and assisted digital support.

evidence.claim: Recurring time-entry forms, submission tracking, reminders, and approvals can use configured workflows.
In the Netherlands, works council consent can apply to staff-data rules and attendance-monitoring arrangements.
The digest documents a Dutch fine for fingerprint-based employee clocking.

assumptions: A digital-first collection process is used as the mid-size-company baseline; paper-heavy sites need a different baseline.
The {HCM} has usable time-entry and approval features.
The proposed route uses ordinary authenticated entry and collects only necessary time data.
Shares include employee and manager effort, so they do not equal payroll-clerk savings.
Consultation estimates are working-day effort; elapsed consultation time may be longer.
unknowns: How many employees currently use paper timecards or lack individual digital access.
Whether native reminders and status reports are already enabled.
Employee accessibility, language, device, and connectivity needs.
Applicable national rules and existing employee-representative agreements.
research_questions: Which accessible submission patterns work well for shared-device and offline workplaces?
Which native features support delegated entry without obscuring who confirmed the hours?
new_work: Support employees who cannot complete the standard submission route.
Maintain rosters, approval delegates, calendars, and reminder schedules.
Handle failed notifications and access problems.
Review whether reminder frequency creates unnecessary employee burden.

tasks.short: Update payroll records for tax declarations, transfers, and departures.

steps.what: Retrieve approved employee changes from the {HCM}.
Check supporting documents for required fields, approval, and effective dates.
Determine the payroll treatment and authorise the record amendment.
Enter the authorised changes into the employee record in the {PAYROLL}.
Compare the updated record against the authorised amendment and check payroll impact.
File the supporting evidence and change verification in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Structured change forms in the {HCM} require effective dates, supporting evidence, and upstream approval; configured rules prepare the payroll amendment for the authorised clerk. After approval, a deterministic integration updates the {PAYROLL}, verifies the written fields and calculation impact, and files evidence in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate employee and payroll records created repeated entry. Effective-date conventions, ownership of fields, and incomplete change requests made direct synchronisation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms, validation rules, and controlled imports already exist. AI-assisted coding can speed field mapping, duplicate protection, and verification without interpreting employment decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, overlapping amendments, tax treatment, and final-pay effects require payroll expertise. National rules and collective agreements vary.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk recognises when a valid HR change has an unusual payroll consequence and obtains a justified treatment before it affects pay.

ambition.what: Daily decisions on effective-date conflicts before payroll cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying employee details to resolving change conflicts and unusual payroll effects. Proposed new authority is to return incomplete requests directly to their originator; compensation and termination decisions retain their existing approvers.

reach.task: Coordinate transfers and departures with complete, effective-dated employee records.
reach.learn: Employee-lifecycle controls, data ownership, and dependencies between contract changes and payroll.

evidence.claim: Structured employee changes can be validated, approved, transferred, and verified using deterministic workflows.
Nmbrs provides checks on salary changes, supporting automated verification of change impact.
GDPR requires appropriate controls for processing employee personal data.

assumptions: The {HCM} holds approved employment facts and the {PAYROLL} holds payroll-specific treatment.
Required values can be captured in structured fields; legacy free-text requests remain exceptions.
The authorised payroll clerk may approve routine record amendments within existing limits.
Verification warnings enter the payroll discrepancy process before pay-run approval.
Build ranges assume one principal employee-record integration and are not measured delivery commitments.
unknowns: Which fields are authoritative in each system and who may approve changes.
Whether supported write interfaces preserve effective dates and historical records.
Volume of retroactive changes, rescinded departures, and overlapping amendments.
Applicable national consultation requirements and approved retention schedules.
research_questions: Which supported integration methods preserve effective-dated history and allow safe retries?
Which payroll checks detect conflicting changes before they affect a pay run?
new_work: Resolve rejected, incomplete, and conflicting change requests.
Maintain field mappings, approval limits, and effective-date rules.
Monitor failed transfers and verify recovery without duplicate amendments.
Review access permissions and retain linked approval evidence.

role.altitude: The role becomes more focused on payroll exceptions, employee support, and coordination across HR and finance. Proposed decision rights cover returning incomplete requests and assigning reconciliation cases; pay changes and payment release follow explicit existing authority.
reach: Human resources specialist: coordinate effective-dated employee changes.
Compensation and benefits specialist: investigate recurring pay-component differences.
Labor relations specialist: support evidence-based resolution of working-time disputes.
Human resources assistant: provide accessible self-service support.
skills_to_grow: Payroll controls and effective-dated record handling.
Integration monitoring, access control, and exception analysis.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early payroll assurance service: surface unresolved time, employee-change, and cash-settlement issues before cutoff, with evidence and a named decision owner for each case.
